title: What are the best AI games you've played?
author: SpicyBoyEnthusiast
selftext:
We hear about slop all the time. I see it everyday. So many devs think because they can make games now they're going to automatically be good. Despite this, I have played a couple really fun ones. I haven't played any great ones.

What's the best AI game you've played? What was good about it? What lessons did you take away?

replies.author: SpicyBoyEnthusiast
replies.body: That game used AI? For art or coding or what?

replies.author: Lambisexual
replies.body:
I think it's mostly a joke. Cause to my recollection, there was a single insignificant poster that seemed to have AI used on it, most likely as a placeholder. It was so insignificant that most people undoubtedly missed it. But it became a big controversy, and so they patched it and said it was only meant to be a placeholder.

As far as we know, the game other than that doesn't use AI.

replies.author: SpicyBoyEnthusiast
replies.body: Lol I mean all of our games, right?

replies.author: iternet
replies.body: Exactly. We'll eventually reach a point where games look identical, and it'll be impossible to prove who copied whom. Only the early creators will make money, but eventually, even they won't get anything for their "efforts"

comments.author: One_Salty_Pigeon
comments.body: Probably the ones you don't even realize are using AI tbh. They feel like just another game. I feel like if you can tell it's AI that's not usually a good sign unless maybe it's certain artwork etc or stuff like that that's always obvious.

replies.author: SpicyBoyEnthusiast
replies.body: Yeah, I got a lot of good feedback on the game Im working on now except for the art and the anti AI crowd clocked the art and hated hard.

replies.author: One_Salty_Pigeon
replies.body: I've started marketing my game and I've already got a few. I typically troll them more often then not. But it's also kind of my brand to be witty and abrasive in a comical way. Otherwise I'd just ignore them. If they want to stay in the stone age let them.
Use humans for the art & music, code assisted games are much more acceptable imo

comments.author: MrDankyStanky
comments.body: My game coded with 100% AI has a Discord with 11.5k people, and Instagram at almost 25k. I started development a little over a month ago, I've made $2k+ in donations already. Shits been insane.

replies.author: SpicyBoyEnthusiast
replies.body: You should do an AMA. In curious how you drummed up that kind of buzz

replies.author: MrDankyStanky
replies.body: I would be down but I feel like every time I mention it here people aren't too interested. Feels more like competition maybe? Idk.

replies.author: VR38DET
replies.body: Do you mind sharing what your game is?

comments.author: iternet
comments.body: Best is my game which is still not released. Exist only in my top-secret plan.

comments.author: Valentinevandal1986
comments.body: I dunno, I enjoyed my own but I think that’s the point. We can make whatever games we want so there’s always a bias

comments.author: Juzzaman
comments.body: There is Eternal War from Purri Cat Studio, but there are some other good upcoming ones too

comments.author: landocs
comments.body: this might be a bit different from a traditional game, but [Human or Not’s group chat](https://humanornot.so/group-chat?utm_source=chatgpt.com) is a fun social experiment where you chat with people and try to figure out who’s actually AI. it’s a good example of using AI to create an interesting challenge rather than just generating content.
